					<div id="mw-content-text" class="mw-body-content"><div class="mw-content-ltr mw-parser-output" lang="en" dir="ltr" data-mw-parsoid-version="0.24.0.0-alpha24" data-mw-html-version="2.8.0"><section data-mw-section-id="0" id="mwAQ"><div class="shortdescription nomobile noexcerpt noprint searchaux" style="display:none" about="#mwt1" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwAg" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"Short description","href":"./Template:Short_description"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"Visual perception under low-light conditions"}},"i":0}}]}">Visual perception under low-light conditions</div><span class="mw-empty-elt" about="#mwt1"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_with_short_description"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Short_description_is_different_from_Wikidata"></span>

<p id="mwAw">In <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vision_science" title="Vision science" id="mwBA">vision science</a>, <b id="mwBQ">scotopic vision</b> or <b id="mwBg">scotopia</b> is the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_perception" title="Visual perception" id="mwBw">visual perception</a> of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyes" title="Eyes" class="mw-redirect" id="mwCA">eyes</a> under <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darkness" title="Darkness" id="mwCQ">low-light</a> conditions.<sup about="#mwt4" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-1"}}"><a href="#cite_note-1" id="mwCg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwCw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDA">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwDQ">]</span></span></a></sup> The term comes from the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek" title="Ancient Greek" id="mwDg">Greek</a> <i id="mwDw">skotos</i>, meaning 'darkness', and <i id="mwEA">-opia</i>, meaning 'a condition of sight'.<sup about="#mwt7" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-2"}}"><a href="#cite_note-2" id="mwEQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwEg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwEw">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwFA">]</span></span></a></sup> In the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_eye" title="Human eye" id="mwFQ">human eye</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cone_cell" title="Cone cell" id="mwFg">cone cells</a> are nonfunctional in low <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visible_spectrum" title="Visible spectrum" id="mwFw">visible light</a>. Scotopic vision is produced exclusively through <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rod_cell" title="Rod cell" id="mwGA">rod cells</a>, which are most <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosensitivity_in_humans" title="Photosensitivity in humans" id="mwGQ">sensitive</a> to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavelength" title="Wavelength" id="mwGg">wavelengths</a> of around 498<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwGw"> </span>nm (blue-green)<sup about="#mwt10" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Bowmaker1980_3-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref mw:Error" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Bowmaker1980","}":""},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Bowmaker1980-3"},"errors":[{"key":"cite_error_ref_too_many_keys","params":["}","dir, follow, group, name"]}]}"><a href="#cite_note-Bowmaker1980-3" id="mwHA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwHQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwHg">[</span>3<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwHw">]</span></span></a></sup> and are insensitive to wavelengths longer than about 640<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwIA"> </span>nm.<sup about="#mwt13" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-4"}}"><a href="#cite_note-4" id="mwIQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwIg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwIw">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwJA">]</span></span></a></sup> Under scotopic conditions, light incident on the retina is not encoded in terms of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectral_power_distribution" title="Spectral power distribution" id="mwJQ">spectral power distribution</a>. Higher visual perception occurs under scotopic vision as it does under <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photopic_vision" title="Photopic vision" id="mwJg">photopic vision</a>.<sup about="#mwt14" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-McKyton_Elul_Levin_2024_p._108929_5-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"McKyton Elul Levin 2024 p. 108929"}}"><a href="#cite_note-McKyton_Elul_Levin_2024_p._108929-5" id="mwJw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwKA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKQ">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwKg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" id="mwKw" data-mw="{"autoGenerated":true}"></section><section data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwLA" aria-labelledby="Retinal_circuitry"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Retinal_circuitry">Retinal circuitry</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Scotopic_vision&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Retinal circuitry"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>

<p id="mwLQ">Of the two types of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photoreceptor_cell" title="Photoreceptor cell" id="mwLg">photoreceptor cells</a> in the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina" title="Retina" id="mwLw">retina</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rod_cell" title="Rod cell" id="mwMA">rods</a> dominate scotopic vision. This dominance is due to the increased sensitivity of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photopigment" title="Photopigment" id="mwMQ">photopigment</a> molecule expressed in rods, as opposed to those in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cone_cell" title="Cone cell" id="mwMg">cones</a>. Rods signal light increments to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina_bipolar_cells" title="Retina bipolar cells" class="mw-redirect" id="mwMw">rod bipolar cells</a> which, unlike most types of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bipolar_cell" title="Bipolar cell" class="mw-redirect" id="mwNA">bipolar cells</a>, do not form direct connections with <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinal_ganglion_cells" title="Retinal ganglion cells" class="mw-redirect" id="mwNQ">retinal ganglion cells</a> – the output neurons of the retina. Instead, two types of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amacrine_cell" title="Amacrine cell" id="mwNg">amacrine cell</a> – <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AII_amacrine_cells" title="AII amacrine cells" id="mwNw">AII</a> and A17 – allow lateral information flow from rod bipolar cells to cone bipolar cells, which in turn contact ganglion cells. Thus, rod signals, mediated by amacrine cells, dominate scotopic vision.<sup about="#mwt17" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-6"}}"><a href="#cite_note-6" id="mwOA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwOQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwOg">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwOw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="2" id="mwPA" aria-labelledby="Occurrence"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Occurrence">Occurrence</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Scotopic_vision&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: Occurrence"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwPQ">Scotopic vision occurs at <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luminance" title="Luminance" id="mwPg">luminance</a> levels of 10<sup id="mwPw">−3</sup><sup about="#mwt21" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-7" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-7"}}"><a href="#cite_note-7" id="mwQA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwQQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwQg">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwQw">]</span></span></a></sup> to 10<sup id="mwRA">−6</sup><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_with_unsourced_statements" about="#mwt18" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwRQ" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"citation needed","href":"./Template:Citation_needed"},"params":{"date":{"wt":"January 2016"}},"i":0}}]}"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_with_unsourced_statements_from_January_2016" about="#mwt18"><sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;" about="#mwt18" id="mwRg"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (January 2016)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candela" title="Candela" id="mwRw">cd</a>/m<sup id="mwSA">2</sup>. Other species are not universally color blind in low-light conditions. The elephant hawk-moth (<i id="mwSQ"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deilephila_elpenor" title="Deilephila elpenor" id="mwSg">Deilephila elpenor</a></i>) displays advanced color discrimination even in dim starlight.<sup about="#mwt24" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-8" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-8"}}"><a href="#cite_note-8" id="mwSw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwTA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwTQ">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwTg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwTw"><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesopic_vision" title="Mesopic vision" id="mwUA">Mesopic vision</a> occurs in intermediate lighting conditions (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luminance" title="Luminance" id="mwUQ">luminance</a> level 10<sup id="mwUg">−3</sup> to 10<sup id="mwUw">0.5</sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candela" title="Candela" id="mwVA">cd</a>/m<sup id="mwVQ">2</sup>)<link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_with_unsourced_statements" about="#mwt25" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwVg" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"Citation needed","href":"./Template:Citation_needed"},"params":{"date":{"wt":"May 2021"}},"i":0}}]}"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_with_unsourced_statements_from_May_2021" about="#mwt25"><sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;" about="#mwt25" id="mwVw"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (May 2021)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup> and is effectively a combination of scotopic and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photopic_vision" title="Photopic vision" id="mwWA">photopic vision</a>. This gives inaccurate <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_acuity" title="Visual acuity" id="mwWQ">visual acuity</a> and color discrimination.</p>

<p id="mwWg">In normal light (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luminance" title="Luminance" id="mwWw">luminance</a> level 10 to 10<sup id="mwXA">8</sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candela" title="Candela" id="mwXQ">cd</a>/m<sup id="mwXg">2</sup>), the vision of cone cells dominates and is <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photopic_vision" title="Photopic vision" id="mwXw">photopic vision</a>. There is good visual acuity (VA) and color discrimination.</p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="3" id="mwYA" aria-labelledby="Wavelength_sensitivity"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Wavelength_sensitivity">Wavelength sensitivity</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Scotopic_vision&action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section: Wavelength sensitivity"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwYQ"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CIE_1951_scotopic_luminosity_function.svg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwYg"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CIE_1951_scotopic_luminosity_function.svg" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/CIE_1951_scotopic_luminosity_function.svg/330px-CIE_1951_scotopic_luminosity_function.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/CIE_1951_scotopic_luminosity_function.svg/960px-CIE_1951_scotopic_luminosity_function.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="600" data-file-height="400" data-file-type="drawing" height="200" width="300" class="mw-file-element" id="mwYw"></a><figcaption id="mwZA">The CIE 1951 scotopic <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luminosity_function" title="Luminosity function" class="mw-redirect" id="mwZQ">luminosity function</a>. The horizontal axis is <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavelength" title="Wavelength" id="mwZg">wavelength</a> in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanometer" title="Nanometer" class="mw-redirect" id="mwZw">nm</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwaA">The normal human observer's relative wavelength sensitivity will not change due to background illumination under scotopic vision. The wavelength sensitivity is determined by the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodopsin" title="Rhodopsin" id="mwaQ">rhodopsin</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photopigment" title="Photopigment" id="mwag">photopigment</a>. This is a red pigment seen at the back of the eye in animals that have a white background to their eye called <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapetum_lucidum" title="Tapetum lucidum" id="mwaw">Tapetum lucidum</a>. The pigment is not noticeable under <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photopic" title="Photopic" class="mw-redirect" id="mwbA">photopic</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesopic" title="Mesopic" class="mw-redirect" id="mwbQ">mesopic</a> conditions.  The principle that the wavelength sensitivity does not change during scotopic vision led to the ability to detect two functional cone classes in individuals.  If two cone classes are present, then their relative sensitivity will change the behavioral wavelength sensitivity.  Therefore, experimentation can determine "the presence of two cone classes by measuring wavelength sensitivity on two different backgrounds and noting a change in the observer's relative wavelength sensitivity."<sup about="#mwt26" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-auto_9-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"auto"}}"><a href="#cite_note-auto-9" id="mwbg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwbw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwcA">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwcQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwcg">The behavior of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodopsin" title="Rhodopsin" id="mwcw">rhodopsin</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photopigment" title="Photopigment" id="mwdA">photopigment</a> explains why the human eye cannot resolve lights with different spectral power distributions under low light.  The reaction of this single photopigment will give the same quanta for 400<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwdQ"> </span>nm light and 700<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwdg"> </span>nm light.  Therefore, this photopigment only maps the rate of absorption and does not encode information about the relative spectral composition of the light.<sup about="#mwt27" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-auto_9-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"auto"}}"><a href="#cite_note-auto-9" id="mwdw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mweA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mweQ">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mweg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwew">In scientific literature, one occasionally encounters the term <i id="mwfA">scotopic lux</i> which corresponds to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photopic_lux" title="Photopic lux" class="mw-redirect" id="mwfQ">photopic lux</a>, but uses instead the scotopic visibility weighting function.<sup about="#mwt32" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-10" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-10"}}"><a href="#cite_note-10" id="mwfg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwfw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwgA">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwgQ">]</span></span></a></sup> The scotopic luminosity function is a standard function established by the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_Internationale_de_l'Éclairage" title="Commission Internationale de l'Éclairage" class="mw-redirect" id="mwgg">Commission Internationale de l'Éclairage</a> (CIE) and standardized in collaboration with the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Organization_for_Standardization" title="International Organization for Standardization" id="mwgw">ISO</a>.<sup about="#mwt35" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-11" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-11"}}"><a href="#cite_note-11" id="mwhA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwhQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwhg">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwhw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwiA">The maximum scotopic efficacy is 1700 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lm/W" title="Lm/W" class="mw-redirect" id="mwiQ">lm/W</a> at 507<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwig"> </span>nm (compared with 683 lm/W at 555<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwiw"> </span>nm for maximum photopic efficacy).<sup about="#mwt38" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-scotopic_efficacy_12-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"scotopic efficacy"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-scotopic_efficacy-12"}}"><a href="#cite_note-scotopic_efficacy-12" id="mwjA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwjQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwjg">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwjw">]</span></span></a></sup> While the ratio between scotopic and photopic efficacies is only around 2.5 counted at peak sensitivity the ratio increases strongly below 500<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwkA"> </span>nm.</p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="4" id="mwkQ" aria-labelledby="Resolution"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Resolution">Resolution</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Scotopic_vision&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Resolution"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwkg">For adaptation to occur at very low levels, the human eye needs to have a large sample of light across the signal in order to get a reliable image. This leads to the human eye being unable to resolve high <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spatial_frequency" title="Spatial frequency" id="mwkw">spatial frequencies</a> in low light since the observer is spatially averaging the light signal.<sup about="#mwt41" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-auto_9-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"auto"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-auto-9"}}"><a href="#cite_note-auto-9" id="mwlA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwlQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwlg">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwlw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwmA">Another reason that vision is poor under scotopic vision is that rods, which are the only cells active under scotopic vision, converge to a smaller number of neurons in the retina. This many-to-one ratio leads to poor <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spatial_frequency" title="Spatial frequency" id="mwmQ">spatial frequency</a> sensitivity.<sup about="#mwt42" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-auto_9-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"auto"}}"><a href="#cite_note-auto-9" id="mwmg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwmw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwnA">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwnQ">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="5" id="mwng" aria-labelledby="General_perception"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="General_perception">General perception</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Scotopic_vision&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: General perception"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwnw">High-level visual perception is similar with scotopic as with photopic sight with people <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reading" title="Reading" id="mwoA">reading</a> with unimpaired  accuracy (though twice as long <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fixation_(visual)" title="Fixation (visual)" id="mwoQ">fixations</a>), able to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face_perception" title="Face perception" id="mwog">recognize faces</a>, and show a <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face_inversion_effect" title="Face inversion effect" id="mwow">face inversion effect</a>.<sup about="#mwt45" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-McKyton_Elul_Levin_2024_p._108929_5-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"McKyton Elul Levin 2024 p. 108929"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-McKyton_Elul_Levin_2024_p._108929-5"}}"><a href="#cite_note-McKyton_Elul_Levin_2024_p._108929-5" id="mwpA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwpQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwpg">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwpw">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
